key_insight: θ-TaN is strongly anisotropic in tension: the c-axis is stronger and stiffer, while the a-axis is more ductile before brittle cleavage fracture.
engineering_relevance: These results help estimate the reliability of θ-TaN for high-thermal-conductivity interconnects and thermal-management components under directional loading.
method: Neuroevolution-potential molecular dynamics for tensile simulations
Size-convergence testing with a 20 nm model
Strain-rate and temperature sweeps to map anisotropic response
evidence_signal: The abstract reports <3.5% variation across 10^7–10^9 s^-1 strain rates and a clear directional split in strength/modulus/failure strain, with fracture controlled by cleavage-plane selection.
watch_item: The conclusions come from high-rate MD conditions, so direct transfer to experimental or service-time loading may require additional validation.
paper_title: Anisotropic Tensile Strength and Fracture Mechanism of $θ$-TaN: A Machine-Learning Potential Molecular Dynamics Study
